Thermal indices from monthly climatology rasters

Source: R/thermify_rast.R
thermify_rast.Rd

Spatial version of thermify() for 12-layer monthly SpatRaster stacks (for example WorldClim 2.1 tmin and tmax). Rasters are processed in blocks of rows: for each block, valid cells are densified to daily values, hourly temperatures are reconstructed when needed, indices are computed and only the aggregated layers are written to disk. Daily or hourly rasters are never held for the whole extent.

Usage

thermify_rast(
  tmin,
  tmax,
  output_dir,
  year = 2023,
  latitude = NULL,
  temporal = c("auto", "tempify", "native"),
  interpolation = "pchip_mp",
  consistency = c("check", "mean_range"),
  indices = c("gdd", "ch", "cu", "cp"),
  gdd_methods = c("average", "single_sine"),
  base = c(5, 10),
  upper = NULL,
  cutoff = "horizontal",
  ch_methods = "sine",
  ch_lower = 0,
  ch_upper = 7.2,
  hourly_method = c("linvill", "sine"),
  chill_period = c("05-01", "08-31"),
  heat_period = c("09-01", "04-30"),
  temporal_aggregation = c("season", "annual", "monthly"),
  max_cells = 2000L,
  format = "GTiff",
  keep_daily = FALSE,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  progress = getOption("thermify.progress", interactive())
)

Arguments

tmin, tmax

SpatRaster objects with 12 layers (January to December) in degrees Celsius and identical geometry.

output_dir

Directory for the output files (created if needed).

year

Reference calendar year for monthly input. Default 2023.

latitude

Optional fixed latitude for the Linvill model. By default the latitude of each cell centre is used (cells are projected to EPSG:4326 when the CRS is not geographic).

temporal

Densification engine for monthly input: "auto", "tempify" or "native" (see densify_monthly()).

interpolation

Densification method, default "pchip_mp".

consistency

"check" or "mean_range" (see densify_monthly()).

indices

Any of "gdd", "ch", "cu", "cp".

gdd_methods

GDD methods, see degree_days(); "hourly" uses degree_hours() on observed or reconstructed hourly temperatures.

base

Lower GDD thresholds (degrees Celsius); one result per value.

upper, cutoff

Upper GDD threshold and cutoff (see degree_days()).

ch_methods

Chilling-hours methods: "sine", "triangle" (from daily extremes) and/or "hourly" (counted on hourly temperatures).

ch_lower, ch_upper

Chilling interval (degrees Celsius).

hourly_method

Hourly reconstruction, "linvill" or "sine".

chill_period, heat_period

Accumulation windows as c("MM-DD", "MM-DD"). Defaults are southern-hemisphere conventions: chill from 1 May to 31 August, heat from 1 September to 30 April.

temporal_aggregation

Any of "season", "annual", "monthly".

max_cells

Maximum number of cells per processing block.

format

"GTiff" and/or "netCDF".

keep_daily

If TRUE, also write the reconstructed daily tmin and tmax (365 or 366 layers each) for diagnosis.

overwrite

Overwrite existing files.

progress

Show progress (blocks done, percentage, elapsed time and estimated time remaining). Defaults to the option thermify.progress, or TRUE in interactive sessions. In non-interactive runs a status line is written at most every 10 seconds, so logs show the process is alive.

Value

A named list of file-backed SpatRaster objects, one per index key, with attribute "provenance".

Outputs

One GeoTIFF per index key (for example gdd_single_sine_b10.tif) is written to output_dir, with layers named after the temporal aggregation: season (accumulation period), annual (1 January to 31 December, GDD and chilling hours only) and m01...m12 (monthly totals; for Utah and Dynamic models only months inside the chill period are filled). The CRS, extent, resolution and NA mask of tmin are preserved. With format = "netCDF" the same layers are also written to one NetCDF file per index. A provenance.json (or .txt without jsonlite) file records parameters and versions.

Memory

Peak memory is roughly proportional to max_cells times the number of hours in a year (8760 values per cell) when hourly-based indices are requested. Lower max_cells to reduce memory; results do not depend on the block size.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)) {
  r <- terra::rast(nrows = 3, ncols = 3, nlyrs = 12,
                   xmin = -72.4, xmax = -72.3, ymin = -36, ymax = -35.9)
  base_min <- c(11, 11, 9, 7, 5, 4, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10)
  base_max <- c(29, 29, 26, 22, 17, 14, 13, 15, 18, 21, 25, 28)
  tmin <- terra::setValues(r, rep(base_min, each = 9))
  tmax <- terra::setValues(r, rep(base_max, each = 9))
  out <- thermify_rast(tmin, tmax, output_dir = tempfile(),
                       temporal = "native", indices = c("gdd", "cp"),
                       gdd_methods = "single_sine", base = 10)
  out$gdd_single_sine_b10
}
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 3, 3, 14  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 0.03333333, 0.03333333  (x, y)
#> extent      : -72.4, -72.3, -36, -35.9  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : lon/lat WGS 84 (EPSG:4326)
#> source      : gdd_single_sine_b10.tif
#> names       :      season,      annual, m01, m02,        m03,       m04, ...
#> min values  : 1686.064087, 1865.361572, 310, 280, 236.363266, 152.88443, ...
#> max values  : 1686.064087, 1865.361572, 310, 280, 236.363266, 152.88443, ...
#> unit        : degC day
# }
